name: WarpBuild (GitHub Actions runners)

modes.label: macOS runner, Apple M4 Pro / M5 Pro
modes.note: "CI runners are billed on a per-minute basis." hour = $/min x 60. GitHub Actions runners only (job-scoped, ephemeral). Apple-hardware macOS VMs; WarpBuild is the lessor running CI jobs on its own fleet. Hosts are Apple M4 Pro and M5 Pro (pricing page: "macOS M4/M5 Pro"). Snapshot runners do not support macOS.

modes.label: Windows runner, x86-64
modes.note: "CI runners are billed on a per-minute basis." hour = $/min x 60. GitHub Actions runners only (job-scoped, ephemeral). Windows licence baked in (2x the Linux x64 rate for the same size). Snapshot runners do not support Windows.

modes.label: Linux runner, x86-64
modes.note: CI runner. Added 2026-09-28 (missing-providers audit). Re-verified on https://www.warpbuild.com/pricing (x64 $0.004..$0.064/min, arm64 $0.003..$0.048/min, Apple-silicon arm64 $0.08/$0.16/min). "CI runners are billed on a per-minute basis." hour = $/min x 60. GitHub Actions runners only (job-scoped, ephemeral).

modes.label: Linux runner, arm64
modes.note: CI runner. Added 2026-09-28 (missing-providers audit). Re-verified on https://www.warpbuild.com/pricing (x64 $0.004..$0.064/min, arm64 $0.003..$0.048/min, Apple-silicon arm64 $0.08/$0.16/min). "CI runners are billed on a per-minute basis." hour = $/min x 60. GitHub Actions runners only (job-scoped, ephemeral).

modes.label: Linux arm64 runner on Apple silicon (M4 Pro / M5 Pro hardware)
modes.note: "Linux (arm64 on Apple Silicon)" is a separate SKU on warpbuild.com/pricing (2026-09-28): 6 vCPU 14 GB $0.08/min, 12 vCPU 28 GB $0.16/min - deliberately the same price as the macOS M4 Pro runner (same Apple hardware), not a mislabelled macOS regime. hour = $/min x 60. GitHub Actions runners only (job-scoped, ephemeral).

modes.label: macOS 26 sandbox (wb CLI), Apple M4 Pro / M5 Pro

features.persist_path: /Users/runner and /opt/homebrew (saved on pause; sandbox expires 7 days after creation)

modes.note: Launched 2026-10-29 (changelog). "billed per second at the macOS 26 runner rate": warp-macos-26-arm64-6x $0.08/min, 12x $0.16/min; hour = $/min x 60. Paused sandboxes have no compute charge; the saved disk is billed as cache storage, $0.20/GB-month plus $0.0001 per save or restore (not modelled). Pause keeps /Users/runner and /opt/homebrew; it does not keep ~/Library, /tmp, /usr/local, /Applications, processes or memory. "A sandbox lasts 7 days from when you created it, running or paused." Driven through the wb CLI: exec, background commands, fs, pty; wb sbx vnc shows the desktop (2026-11-03). No published concurrency limit. Source: https://www.warpbuild.com/docs/ci/sandboxes

modes.label: Claude Managed Agents self_hosted environment on WarpBuild runners (Linux/macOS)
modes.note: Stock runner labels only (no custom images yet); Windows 'coming soon'. Sessions billed per second. Outputs in /mnt/session/outputs billed as cache ($0.20/GB-month, 7-day TTL after last access). Only usable with Anthropic's Claude Managed Agents harness. Sizes: same presets and $/min as linux-x64, linux-arm64, linux-arm64-apple and macos-m4pro (M4 Pro / M5 Pro) (hour = $/min x 60).

plans.name: Pay as you go
plans.note: No credit card to start; card required "when you hit the free usage or credit limits" (amount unpublished). Unlimited job concurrency on Linux/Windows (macOS per-org quota). Billed on the last day of each month, but accounts past a usage/history threshold may be charged mid-cycle. No refunds for usage-based products. AWS Marketplace billing available (billed daily; no free credits).

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.note: Dedicated cloud, region-specific infra, 99.9% SLA, SCIM. Add-ons on the pricing page: SAML SSO $250/month, Data Residency $250/month, Audit Logs $400/month.

caveats: Mostly a CI-runner product: the five runner modes are flagged alt (machines exist only for a GitHub Actions job). Since 2026-10-29 WarpBuild also sells macOS 26 sandboxes (mode macos-sandbox): pause/resume, VNC desktop, per-second billing, 7-day life from creation.

Add-ons: cache storage $0.20/GB-month, cache write/restore $0.0001/op, snapshot restore $0.04/job, snapshot storage $0.025/hour per snapshot (~$18.25 per snapshot-month) — not per GiB, so snapshot_gib_month is null.
BYOC (your AWS/GCP/Azure): $0.002/min per Linux or Windows runner on top of your own cloud bill; not modelled.
Free usage amount not published. Networking (Tailscale) add-on is free.
macOS on Apple hardware: Apple macOS SLA: leasing a Mac requires a minimum lease of 24 consecutive hours with sole use by the lessee, and allows at most 2 additional macOS VMs per Mac.

Card category is "macos" only because the schema has no CI category; every regime sets product_class "ci-runner" and an explicit os, so Linux/Windows runners are not treated as macOS. All regimes keep flag alt (CI minutes); the engine ignores alt when the workload is shopping for a CI runner.
Snapshot runners: snapshots are auto-deleted after 15 days, so one retained snapshot costs at most ~$9 (360 h x $0.025) unless refreshed.
SSO (SAML 2.0 or OIDC) is self-serve from Settings -> SSO at $250/month, billed after the first domain is verified (was enterprise-contact).
Removed on 2026-06-08: WarpBuild Cloud spot runners, Windows 2 vCPU runners, macOS 13, custom cloud runner configurations (spot now BYOC-only).
macOS memory: 6 vCPU = 22 GB and 12 vCPU = 44 GB until 2026-09-30; from 2026-10-01 14 GB / 28 GB at unchanged prices (card already uses the post-change values).
Docker builders auto-scaling in private beta (2026-09-25); prices unchanged $0.06-$0.88/min.
Add-ons (pricing page, 2026-11-08): Data Residency $250/month, Audit Logs $400/month, SAML SSO $250/month.
macOS sandbox paused disk: billed as cache storage ($0.20/GB-month + $0.0001 per save/restore); not modelled in the hourly price.
Snapshot runners work only on WarpBuild Cloud Ubuntu runners; Windows, macOS and BYOC runners ignore snapshot labels.

fleet.verification: No card initially; pricing says card is needed when free usage/credit limits are reached.
fleet.notes: Pricing advertises unlimited runner concurrency and no queue limit. No separate numeric new-account anti-abuse cap or approval time published. Null is used instead of inventing a finite maximum; stock/operational capacity still not guaranteed. Unlimited concurrency applies to GA features on Linux and Windows only; since 2026-07 the macOS fleet (and the Apple-silicon Linux xfast runners on the same hardware) is capped by an unpublished per-organization quota (raise via support@warpbuild.com); beta features may not have unlimited concurrency.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: The runner always boots from the base image. Use `snapshot-save` action to capture a snapshot at the desired point in your workflow.
snapshot_auto.note: Runners are ephemeral per-job VMs destroyed after the job ('The VMs are created on demand and destroyed after each build'); nothing is saved automatically. Agent-runner sessions persist only /mnt/session/outputs as a cache artifact (7-day TTL), not machine state.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: WarpBuild allows you to take snapshots of your runner VMs at any point during your workflow, enabling faster consecutive runs by reusing these snapshots.
snapshot_on_demand.note: Via WarpBuilds/snapshot-save action inside the job (also Snapshotter API POST/GET/DELETE /snapshots). New runners boot from it with `snapshot.key=<alias>` (45-60 s boot). Disk only as far as documented ('/tmp directory will not persist state since this directory is cleaned on reboots'); no memory. WarpBuild Cloud Ubuntu runners only ("Snapshot Runners are supported only on WarpBuild Cloud Ubuntu runners"; not BYOC/Windows/macOS). Snapshots deleted after 15 days; $0.025/h per snapshot storage + $0.04 per restore.

egress_allowlist.quote: While runners need outbound internet access, you can tighten egress rules.
egress_allowlist.note: BYOC only: security-group egress rules and Network ACLs in YOUR AWS VPC (stack-level SG; import mode lets you pick an existing SG), i.e. IP/CIDR/port level and enforced outside the VM. Default SG 'All egress allowed (`0.0.0.0/0`)'. No egress controls documented for WarpBuild Cloud runners. Tailscale networking addon adds tailnet access (ACL tags), not an egress filter.

ingress_rules.quote: Create a security group that blocks all inbound traffic. This is to ensure that no unauthorized access to the runners is possible.
ingress_rules.note: BYOC: SG inbound rules (default ingress from VPC subnet CIDRs only; RDP 3389 not exposed by default). Cloud runners expose no ports; Action-Debugger SSH via gha.warp.build URL, restricted to the triggering GitHub user's SSH keys when set (`limit-access-to-actor`), otherwise anyone with the URL.

guest_firewall.note: Each runner is its own VM ('Each runner runs in its own virtual machine') with sudo, mirroring GitHub runner images; iptables not mentioned.

secret_proxy.quote: WarpBuild does not access or store any build secrets. Secrets are stored in your source code repository and are only accessible to your runner environment.
secret_proxy.note: GitHub Actions secrets land in the runner env. OIDC tokens (Tailscale addon) / BYOC instance profiles give short-lived cloud creds inside the VM; no credential-injecting proxy.

volume_attach.quote: Each runner has its own encrypted storage volume that is created on demand and destroyed after each build.
volume_attach.note: No attachable persistent volumes. Persistence only via cache (S3-backed, $0.20/GB-month), snapshots, BYOC standby disks (pre-booted pool, not attachable storage), auto-mounted local NVMe on BYOC instance types.

volume_shared.quote: Each runner has its own encrypted storage volume that is created on demand and destroyed after each build.
volume_shared.note: No shared FS; shared state across runners only via cache API / Docker builder cache.

isolation.quote: Each runner runs in its own virtual machine. The virtual machines are created on demand and destroyed after each build, and they are not reused.
isolation.note: WarpBuild describes only 'virtual machine' isolation on its own bare-metal fleet (per its uptime/reliability blog post, primarily bare-metal servers with hyperscaler fallback), not a named microVM technology like Firecracker (that is a competitor, Blacksmith). Nested-virtualization docs expose /dev/kvm to Linux x64 jobs, implying a KVM-based hypervisor for the guest VMs, so 'qemu-kvm' (full VM) is the closest documented fit rather than firecracker/cloud-hypervisor, which WarpBuild never claims for itself.

image_oci.quote: Yes. WarpBuild BYOC runs your own VM images on AWS, GCP, and Azure once they meet the documented requirements, and a custom runner selects the image.
image_oci.note: Custom images are cloud VM images (AMI/GCE image/Azure image) selected for BYOC custom runners, not Docker/OCI images used to start the machine itself; the hosted (non-BYOC) fleet does not accept any customer-supplied image at all.

browser.quote: CI runners are billed on a per-minute basis.
browser.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. WarpBuild sells ephemeral GitHub Actions CI runner VMs; a managed/real browser is not part of the product (users may install/cache Playwright browsers themselves inside a job, but WarpBuild does not provide or manage one).

anti_bot.quote: CI runners are billed on a per-minute basis.
anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. This is a GitHub Actions CI runner product, not a browsing/scraping agent product.

captcha_solving.quote: CI runners are billed on a per-minute basis.
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No CAPTCHA-solving capability is documented anywhere on warpbuild.com; the product is CI compute, not a browser/agent automation service.

egress_ip_type.quote: We prioritize bare metal servers for runners whenever possible... Hyperscalers: Windows runners, ARM64 Linux runners, and Docker builders run on hyperscalers... we primarily use AWS with passive backup stacks on GCP and Azure.
egress_ip_type.note: Runner outbound IPs come from WarpBuild's own colocation bare-metal fleet or AWS/GCP/Azure hyperscaler ranges (or the customer's own cloud account on BYOC) — ordinary datacenter/cloud IP space, not residential or mobile.

wake_on_request.quote: A standby disk is a VM of the runner's instance type, booted once so networking and machine setup complete, then shut down. When GitHub requests a runner, WarpBuild boots one from the pool, which puts job start at roughly 15 seconds.
wake_on_request.note: BYOC-only feature: a pool of pre-warmed, shut-down standby VMs is automatically powered back on when a job request arrives, rather than booting cold. Not available on the hosted/non-BYOC fleet, on Windows/macOS labels, or with Spot instances.

live_resize.quote: Each runner runs in its own virtual machine. The virtual machines are created on demand and destroyed after each build, and they are not reused.
live_resize.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Runners are ephemeral, one VM per job; there is no long-running machine whose CPU/RAM could be changed live — resizing means picking a different runner label/instance type for the next job.

harness_api.quote: WarpBuild hosts a Model Context Protocol server at https://mcp.warpbuild.com/mcp, and an MCP host connected to it can interact with the WarpBuild API to create runners, create runner images, and read what already exists.
harness_api.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. WarpBuild's MCP server/API manages CI runner infrastructure (create runners/images, read job/cost data), not a first-party API that prompts/streams/follow-ups a coding agent harness inside the sandbox. The 'agent-runner' mode only runs Anthropic's own Claude Managed Agents harness on stock runner labels; WarpBuild provides no API of its own to drive that harness.

own_agent_api.quote: CI runners are billed on a per-minute basis.
own_agent_api.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. WarpBuild has no first-party browser/computer-use/research task agent of its own; it only sells GitHub Actions CI compute plus an MCP server/API for managing that CI infrastructure.

lang_python.quote: The Linux x86-64 runner images have the same tooling installed as GitHub-hosted runners, which is why actions/setup-node, actions/setup-python, actions/setup-go, and the rest resolve against preinstalled versions instead of downloading a toolchain on every job.
lang_python.note: Python ships preinstalled on Linux/macOS/Windows runner images, matching GitHub-hosted runner images.

lang_node.quote: Node, Python, Go, Rust, Docker, the AWS CLI, and the rest of the standard inventory are present, so actions/setup-* steps resolve against preinstalled versions instead of downloading them.
lang_node.note: Node.js ships preinstalled on the runner images.

egress_http_rules.quote: While runners need outbound internet access, you can tighten egress rules.
egress_http_rules.note: Egress control is at IP/CIDR/port level via AWS security groups and Network ACLs in the customer's own BYOC VPC (card's own feature_evidence records egress_allowlist_level as 'ip'); no HTTP method/path-level egress rule engine is documented, and the hosted (non-BYOC) fleet has no documented egress controls at all.

hipaa.quote: SOC 2 Type 2 with three Trust Services Criteria: Security, Availability, and Confidentiality.
hipaa.note: WarpBuild's own trust center, security docs, and enterprise pages advertise only SOC 2 Type 2 (plus SAML/OIDC SSO); no HIPAA-eligibility or BAA claim appears anywhere on warpbuild.com, unlike some direct competitors (e.g. Blacksmith states GDPR/HIPAA-in-progress) that the provider's own comparison pages explicitly contrast against WarpBuild's SOC-2-only posture.

eu_data_residency.quote: WarpBuild places GitHub Actions runners in the EU two ways: a hosted EU region on the enterprise tier, or BYOC runners in your own AWS or GCP account.
eu_data_residency.note: Pricing page lists Data Residency as a $250/month add-on; the EU page says hosted EU region on the enterprise tier. BYOC in the customer's own EU cloud region also works. Runner, disk and cache bucket stay in the region (not applicable to macOS).

max_session_h.quote: GitHub's own fleet stops a job at 6 hours. Registered runners get 5 days, and WarpBuild registers itself as a self-hosted runner in the Default runner group (id 1) of your organization... so a WarpBuild job runs under the 5 day ceiling rather than the 6 hour one.
max_session_h.note: WarpBuild runners register with GitHub as self-hosted runners, which GitHub caps at 5 days (120 hours) of job execution, versus the 6-hour cap on GitHub-hosted runners. This is GitHub's platform ceiling that WarpBuild's registration mechanism runs under, not a WarpBuild-published SLA number of its own. macOS sandboxes: "A sandbox lasts 7 days from when you created it, running or paused" (mode max_session_h 168).

persistent_disk.quote: Snapshots are temporary and will be deleted after 15 days.
persistent_disk.how: save a snapshot of the Ubuntu runner disk with snapshot-save and boot the next runner from it with snapshot.key (kept 15 days)
persistent_disk.note: A CI runner disk is still destroyed after each job ("created on demand and destroyed after each build"). macOS sandboxes (mode macos-sandbox) keep the home folder and Homebrew when paused, for at most 7 days from creation: https://www.warpbuild.com/docs/ci/sandboxes

pause_resume.quote: Pausing a sandbox saves its disk and stops it. Resuming starts a new VM from that disk, so your files and the tools you installed are still there.
pause_resume.note: CI runners: no pause/resume (one VM per job). The macos-sandbox mode sets pause_resume true: paused sandboxes have no compute charge, the saved disk bills as cache storage, and the sandbox expires 7 days after creation.

fork.quote: The runner always boots from the base image. Use `snapshot-save` action to capture a snapshot at the desired point in your workflow.
fork.note: Snapshot-runners only let a NEW runner boot from a previously saved disk image later; there is no operation that clones an existing machine into siblings.

fork_running.quote: WarpBuild allows you to take snapshots of your runner VMs at any point during your workflow, enabling faster consecutive runs by reusing these snapshots.
fork_running.note: Snapshot-save happens inside the job that keeps running to completion and is then destroyed; a later, separate runner boots from the saved disk (45-60s cold boot) - not a clone of the still-running machine.

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: The `/tmp` directory will not persist state since this directory is cleaned on reboots
memory_snapshot_fork.note: Snapshots documented as disk-image only; no memory/process-state capture or restore, and no fork API at all.

desktop.quote: See and use your macOS sandbox's desktop.
desktop.note: CI runners have no desktop stream. The macos-sandbox mode sets desktop true: `wb sbx vnc <name> --open` shows the macOS desktop in Screen Sharing (2026-11-03, wb CLI 0.1.3). macOS only; no Linux desktop.

computer_use.quote: wb sbx vnc <name> shows the desktop in a VNC viewer.
computer_use.note: No screenshot+click driving API is documented. The macOS sandbox desktop is reachable over VNC for a person or an agent that brings its own VNC client.

volumes.quote: Each runner has its own encrypted storage volume that is created on demand and destroyed after each build.
volumes.note: No attachable/shared persistent volume product; matches the existing feature_evidence for volume_attach/volume_shared already on the card.

inbound_https.quote: a security group attached to every runner instance that blocks all inbound traffic ... Inbound can be blocked entirely, because the runner agent polls outbound.
inbound_https.note: No public URLs. Runners accept no inbound connections; debug SSH into jobs goes through Action-Debugger (v2 requires a GitHub SSH key, 2026-11-05). Runners can join your tailnet with the free Tailscale add-on. macOS sandboxes give a shell (pty) and VNC through the wb CLI, not an HTTPS URL.

public_ipv4.quote: Block all inbound connections. Runner agents open outbound connections and hold them, so no inbound rule is required for a job to run. Remove every inbound rule from the runner security group.
public_ipv4.note: Even where a BYOC runner sits in a public subnet, no public IPv4 is exposed/documented as a reachable, user-facing address - inbound is uniformly blocked, so there is no supported 'public IPv4 per machine' feature.

static_egress_ip.quote: Static egress IPs for GitHub Actions runners are a BYOC capability on AWS, GCP, and Azure. ... On WarpBuild, static IPs are a BYOC capability on AWS, GCP, and Azure, switched on per custom runner
static_egress_ip.note: CORRECTION: this is a documented first-party feature (opt-in per BYOC custom runner; addresses are the NAT gateway/Cloud NAT elastic IPs). Unavailable on WarpBuild Cloud (non-BYOC) runners, but available overall via BYOC, so the provider-level flag should be true.

agent_harnesses.quote: WarpBuild's Linux and macOS runners can now be the self-hosted execution environment for Claude Managed Agents. ... These same runners can now be the execution environment for Claude Managed Agents.
agent_harnesses.note: CORRECTION: WarpBuild ships a dedicated 'Agent Runners' dashboard/product that runs Anthropic's Claude Managed Agents coding-agent harness on stock WarpBuild runner VMs (any stock Linux/macOS runner is selectable for a session) - a first-party offered integration for a coding agent, matching the card's own 'agent-runner' mode.

gpu.quote: High-performance CI/CD runners that are 2x faster and 50% cheaper than standard GitHub Actions runners.
gpu.note: No 'gpu' mention anywhere across the full docs/blog/guides sitemap (llms.txt, ~830 pages) or the pricing page; only CPU runner sizes (2-32 vCPU) are sold.

self_host.quote: Enterprise-grade GitHub Actions runners with SOC2 compliance, BYOC deployment, SSO, and 99.9% SLA. 40% cheaper than self-hosting on Kubernetes.
self_host.note: WarpBuild positions itself as a managed alternative TO self-hosting (BYOC still means WarpBuild's control plane manages runners in your cloud account); there is no downloadable/self-hostable WarpBuild runner-control-plane software.

open_source.note: Core product is a paid, metered SaaS (per-minute billed runners, paid plans, Enterprise sales) with no published OSI license for the runner platform/control-plane; only a small support utility ("open-source Action Debugger") is separately called out as open source, not the core product.

cpu_class.quote: Dedicated hardware resources for compute-intensive CI/CD workloads. Baremetal Performance: Direct access to high-performance hardware without virtualization overhead for maximum throughput.
cpu_class.note: WarpBuild's x86-64 runner product page explicitly advertises 'dedicated hardware resources' and bare-metal (no virtualization-overhead) access, and its own architecture post (https://www.warpbuild.com/blog/uptime-reliability) says it 'primarily' runs Linux/macOS runners on its own bare-metal fleet with 'complete hardware isolation' and 'nested virtualization to ensure the builder instance is completely isolated from the host' (docker-builders blog: 'Dedicated cores of fast, high single core performance processors'). Each GitHub Actions job also gets a fresh, non-reused VM ('created on demand and destroyed after each build ... not reused'), so there is no cross-job/cross-customer CPU sharing on a given runner. Windows runners and the AWS-Graviton-5-powered ARM64 runners are documented as running on hyperscaler AWS/GCP/Azure instances instead of WarpBuild's own bare metal (per the uptime/reliability blog: 'Hyperscalers: Windows runners, ARM64 Linux runners, and Docker builders run on hyperscalers'); WarpBuild does not publish a separate CPU-sharing statement for those two platforms, so 'dedicated' here is inferred (lower confidence for windows-x64/linux-arm64) from the same per-job-VM, no-reuse lifecycle and the absence of any burstable/shared-vCPU or oversubscription language anywhere in WarpBuild's docs, blog, or pricing pages (unlike Namespace/Blacksmith, who use similar per-job VM models and are treated as full dedicated-VM isolation). macOS (macos-m4pro) and the same-hardware linux-arm64-apple SKU run on real Apple Silicon Mac hardware under Apple's macOS VM licensing terms (minimum 24-consecutive-hour lease with 'sole use by the lessee'), which grants the leasing customer exclusive (not multi-tenant) access to that physical Mac's cores for the lease duration, supporting 'dedicated' rather than 'shared' for those two modes as well, though WarpBuild does not itself publish a CPU-pinning/no-oversubscription guarantee across the up-to-3 concurrent VMs a lessee may run on one Mac.

usage_api.quote: WarpBuild hosts a Model Context Protocol server at https://mcp.warpbuild.com/mcp, and an MCP host connected to it can interact with the WarpBuild API to create runners, create runner images, and read what already exists.
usage_api.note: granularity: per-sandbox; cost: yes; MCP server and WarpBuild API can read job and cost data per runner (per-sandbox granularity); runners are ephemeral per-job VMs.

persist_scope.quote: WarpBuild allows you to take snapshots of your runner VMs at any point during your workflow, enabling faster consecutive runs by reusing these snapshots.
persist_scope.how: run the snapshot-save action in the job, then start the next runner with snapshot.key=<alias> (WarpBuild Cloud Ubuntu runners only; /tmp is not kept)
persist_scope.note: "Snapshots are temporary and will be deleted after 15 days." "Snapshot Runners are supported only on WarpBuild Cloud Ubuntu runners." Windows and macOS runner modes set persist_scope none. The macos-sandbox mode keeps /Users/runner and /opt/homebrew on pause (folder), for at most 7 days from creation. $0.025/h per snapshot storage + $0.04 per restore.

audit_logs.quote: Audit logs record every change made in your WarpBuild organization.
audit_logs.note: Added 2026-10-26; kept 13 months in write-once storage. Add-on at $400/month on https://www.warpbuild.com/pricing.

locations_quote: WarpBuild does not publish a documented list of specific regions or locations where runners are deployed. EU data residency is available on enterprise tier, but the exact region names/cities are not detailed on the pricing page.

audit_2026_11_08.source: findings/warpbuild.json re-checked against warpbuild.com pricing, sandboxes, snapshot-runners and changelog pages
